name: Retail
blurb: Demand forecasting, recommendation, and customer-service automation at volume, with NRF, Coresight, and IHL tracking the deployments.

points.desc: The Census BTOS series reports AI use for retail trade alongside every other sector, updated fortnightly.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The National Retail Federation covers store automation, inventory computer vision, and customer-experience software - the trade body's research is where retail AI adoption gets counted.

summary: Demand forecasting, recommendation, and customer-service automation are the volume use cases.

analysis.body:
The Census BTOS series reports AI use for retail trade, NAICS 44-45, as the share of firms answering yes to whether they used AI in the last two weeks. The latest reading is 15.5%, compared with 15.2% in the prior period, and the question was first asked in September 2023. This is a narrow, recent-use measure, so it captures only firms that deployed AI within that short window.

IHL Group's research page cites several retail deployments. GE Appliances is deploying autonomous vehicles, robotics, AI cameras and sensors, and its Brilliant Factory data platform at its Roper Corp. plant in Georgia, where the tools detect defects, predict equipment failures, optimize staffing and forecast demand. Nature's Emporium has partnered with Retailgrid to strengthen pricing decisions across its Ontario organic and natural-goods stores, using Retailgrid's AI-powered spreadsheet and Price Radar platform to integrate daily sales data, model demand and price elasticity, and track four key natural-products competitors plus Amazon.ca, beginning with the supplements category. Rainbow has opened its upgraded Shahe sp@ce supermarket in Shenzhen, its first Store Digital Twin site, built with Hanshow and Lingzhi Digital Technology, using 17,000 IoT devices, NexConnect Smart Carts, Nebular Ultra ESLs, AI vision, robotics and retail AI to improve navigation, fulfilment, shelf execution and replenishment.

IHL Group's 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, in cooperation with Chain Store Age, finds inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates specialty retail winners from laggards. IHL Group also finds most retail AI budgets fund the wrong layer first, stalling AI pilots before they reach the store floor in 2026. Inventory distortion is down to $1.7 trillion, but empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion. Coresight Research delivers data-driven insights focusing on retail and technology, and leads an invite-only forum exploring AI opportunities and challenges for consumer-focused businesses. Coresight Research produces adoption rates and market sizing for AI in merchandising and supply-chain logistics, though the excerpt does not give a specific figure. Its coverage includes Placer.ai, whose CMO discusses how data and AI are transforming retail strategies, organizational structures, and the future of malls, marketing, and retail innovation.

The same IHL page reports measurable results from Dr. Squatch, which uses AfterShip's AI-powered estimated delivery dates and AfterShip Intelligence on tracking pages, pairing consistent pre- and post-purchase delivery visibility with personalized product recommendations. The brand achieved a 31.89% recommendation click-through rate, attributed $32,978 in Q1 revenue, cut WISMO inquiries 25%, and reached 94% delivery-date accuracy. GE Appliances reports the tools help cut downtime and reduce scrap, while Nature's Emporium and Rainbow describe operational improvements in pricing, navigation, fulfilment, shelf execution and replenishment, though without specific percentages in the excerpt.

The National Retail Federation tracks store technology and policy. NRF says digital pricing tools are suited to today's fast-moving, competitive marketplace and provide greater efficiency and accuracy in pricing, but it also notes that lawmakers scrutinize retail technology, and understanding how retailers use data, discounts and digital pricing tools is critical to informed policymaking. New Jersey's "fair share" law raises health care, compliance and privacy concerns for retailers and other employers. NRF continues to ask Congress to provide federal support against organized retail crime, and its policy issues include credit card swipe fees, immigration and tariffs. The CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor, powered by Affinity Solutions, showed retail sales rose again in July, marking the 10th consecutive month of gains.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the measured adoption rate is 15.5%, compared with 15.2% in the prior period, and the question covers only the last two weeks. IHL's finding that inventory data accuracy, not AI budget size, separates winners from laggards points to data foundations as a precondition. NRF's policy coverage signals rising scrutiny of digital pricing and data practices, with compliance and privacy concerns already appearing in state law. Coresight Research and IHL Group both track deployments and market sizing, but the excerpts do not provide a single retail-wide ROI figure, so decisions should rest on the specific use cases and vendor results reported here.

https://nrf.com/.brief: The National Retail Federation presents itself as an advocate for the people, policies, and ideas that support retail, and it provides news, insights, and industry events. Its featured events include NRF 2027: Retail’s Big Show, the Retail Law Summit, and NRF PROTECT, alongside centers for retail insights, digital risk, sustainability, and small business. According to the CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor powered by Affinity Solutions, retail sales increased again in July, the tenth straight monthly gain. The organization states that digital pricing tools fit today’s fast-moving competitive market and offer greater pricing efficiency and accuracy. NRF also says it focuses on policy issues such as organized retail crime, credit card swipe fees, immigration, and tariffs.

https://ihlservices.com/.brief: IHL Group conducts research on retail technology spending and strategy. According to their 2026 study of 96 specialty retail brands, inventory data accuracy rather than AI budget size determines which specialty retailers succeed, and most retail AI budgets fund the wrong infrastructure layer first. The organisation also reports that inventory distortion has declined to $1.7 trillion, though empty shelves still cost $690.9 billion annually. IHL's analysis finds that the presence of AI does not predict pricing-platform quality among vendors, and retailers should instead evaluate explainability, automation controls, and governance safeguards.
